pages.caption: Once upon a time, in a very far-off country, there lived a merchant who had been so fortunate in all his undertakings that he was enormously rich.
pages.description: [A merchant with twelve children in a grand mansion]
pages.scene: A merchant with twelve children in a grand mansion

pages.caption: But one day a most unexpected misfortune befell them.
pages.description: [A great fire engulfing a mansion at night]
pages.scene: A great fire engulfing a mansion at night

pages.caption: Their father, who had until this moment prospered in all ways, suddenly lost every ship he had upon the sea.
pages.description: [A merchant at a dock, watching ships sink in a storm]
pages.scene: A merchant at a dock, watching ships sink in a storm

pages.caption: All that he had left was a little house in a desolate place at least a hundred leagues from the town in which he had lived.
pages.description: [A small cottage in a dark, desolate forest]
pages.scene: A small cottage in a dark, desolate forest

pages.caption: As they were too poor to have any servants, the girls had to work hard, like peasants.
pages.description: [Six daughters scrubbing and working in a humble cottage]
pages.scene: Six daughters scrubbing and working in a humble cottage

pages.caption: Only the youngest tried to be brave and cheerful.
pages.description: [A young woman with a kind smile, singing cheerfully while her sisters scowl]
pages.scene: A young woman with a kind smile, singing cheerfully while her sisters scowl

pages.caption: She was really far prettier and cleverer than they were; indeed, she was so lovely that she was always called Beauty.
pages.description: [The youngest daughter, beautiful and serene, standing apart from her sisters]
pages.scene: The youngest daughter, beautiful and serene, standing apart from her sisters

pages.caption: Their father received the news that one of his ships, which he had believed to be lost, had come safely into port with a rich cargo.
pages.description: [A merchant receiving a letter at the cottage door]
pages.scene: A merchant receiving a letter at the cottage door

pages.caption: So they all loaded their father with commissions for jewels and dresses which it would have taken a fortune to buy.
pages.description: [Six sisters excitedly piling presents and jewels around their father]
pages.scene: Six sisters excitedly piling presents and jewels around their father

pages.caption: Only Beauty, feeling sure that it was of no use, did not ask for anything.
pages.description: [Beauty standing quietly while her sisters clamor for gifts]
pages.scene: Beauty standing quietly while her sisters clamor for gifts

pages.caption: "And what shall I bring for you, Beauty?"
pages.description: [The merchant looking at Beauty with tenderness]
pages.scene: The merchant looking at Beauty with tenderness

pages.caption: "The only thing I wish for is to see you come home safely," she answered.
pages.description: [Beauty smiling gently at her father]
pages.scene: Beauty smiling gently at her father

pages.caption: "Well, dear father, as you insist upon it, I beg that you will bring me a rose.
pages.description: [Beauty asking her father for a single rose]
pages.scene: Beauty asking her father for a single rose

pages.caption: So the merchant set out and reached the town as quickly as possible, but only to find that his former companions, believing him to be dead, had divided between them the goods which the ship had brought.
pages.description: [A merchant on horseback riding through a winter storm]
pages.scene: A merchant on horseback riding through a winter storm

pages.caption: Not a house was to be seen; the only shelter he could get was the hollow trunk of a great tree, and there he crouched all the night.
pages.description: [A merchant crouching inside a hollow tree trunk at night]
pages.scene: A merchant crouching inside a hollow tree trunk at night

pages.caption: At length he made out some sort of track, and it presently became easier, and led him into an avenue of trees which ended in a splendid castle.
pages.description: [A merchant discovering a magnificent palace hidden in the woods]
pages.scene: A merchant discovering a magnificent palace hidden in the woods

pages.caption: Deep silence reigned everywhere, and at last, tired of roaming through empty rooms and galleries, he stopped in a room smaller than the rest.
pages.description: [A merchant walking through empty, lavish palace rooms]
pages.scene: A merchant walking through empty, lavish palace rooms

pages.caption: Thinking that this must be prepared for someone who was expected, he sat down to wait, and very soon fell into a sweet sleep.
pages.description: [A merchant sleeping by a warm fire in a cozy room]
pages.scene: A merchant sleeping by a warm fire in a cozy room

pages.caption: When his extreme hunger wakened him after several hours, he was still alone; but a little table, upon which was a good dinner, had been drawn up close to him.
pages.description: [A merchant waking to find a table full of food]
pages.scene: A merchant waking to find a table full of food

pages.caption: Then he went down into the garden, and though it was winter everywhere else, here the sun shone, and the birds sang, and the flowers bloomed.
pages.description: [A merchant wandering through a lush garden full of roses in winter]
pages.scene: A merchant wandering through a lush garden full of roses in winter

pages.caption: This path had a hedge of roses on each side of it, and the merchant thought he had never seen or smelt such exquisite flowers.
pages.description: [A merchant reaching for a beautiful rose in the hedge]
pages.scene: A merchant reaching for a beautiful rose in the hedge

pages.caption: Turning round, he saw a frightful Beast, which seemed to be very angry and said, in a terrible voice: "Who told you that you might gather my roses?"
pages.description: [A fearsome Beast roaring with fury behind the merchant]
pages.scene: A fearsome Beast roaring with fury behind the merchant

pages.caption: The merchant, terrified by these furious words, dropped the fatal rose, and, throwing himself on his knees, cried: "Pardon me, noble sir."
pages.description: [A merchant kneeling before the Beast in terror]
pages.scene: A merchant kneeling before the Beast in terror

pages.caption: "You are very ready with excuses and flattery," he cried; "but that will not save you from the death you deserve."
pages.description: [The Beast looming over the trembling merchant]
pages.scene: The Beast looming over the trembling merchant

pages.caption: And in despair he began to tell the Beast all his misfortunes, and the reason of his journey, not forgetting to mention Beauty's request.
pages.description: [A merchant weeping as he tells the Beast about his daughter]
pages.scene: A merchant weeping as he tells the Beast about his daughter

pages.caption: The Beast considered for a moment, and then he said, in a less furious tone: "I will forgive you on one condition--that is, that you will give me one of your daughters."
pages.description: [The Beast considering the merchant with a stern expression]
pages.scene: The Beast considering the merchant with a stern expression

pages.caption: "Ah!" cried the merchant, "if I were cruel enough to buy my own life at the expense of one of my children's, what excuse could I invent to bring her here?"
pages.description: [A merchant begging on his knees before the Beast]
pages.scene: A merchant begging on his knees before the Beast

pages.caption: "No excuse would be necessary," answered the Beast. "If she comes at all she must come willingly.
pages.description: [The Beast pointing a clawed finger at the merchant]
pages.scene: The Beast pointing a clawed finger at the merchant

pages.caption: "I give you a month to see if either of your daughters will come back with you and stay here, to let you go free."
pages.description: [The Beast gesturing toward the door of the palace]
pages.scene: The Beast gesturing toward the door of the palace

pages.caption: The merchant was only too glad when the Beast went away, and though he could not sleep for sadness, he lay down until the sun rose.
pages.description: [The merchant departing the palace on horseback with a rose]
pages.scene: The merchant departing the palace on horseback with a rose

pages.caption: He hid the truth from them at first, only saying sadly to Beauty as he gave her the rose: "Here is what you asked me to bring you; you little know what it has cost."
pages.description: [The merchant arriving home at the cottage, giving Beauty the rose]
pages.scene: The merchant arriving home at the cottage, giving Beauty the rose

pages.caption: But this excited their curiosity so greatly that presently he told them his adventures from beginning to end, and then they were all very unhappy.
pages.description: [The merchant recounting his tale to his horrified family]
pages.scene: The merchant recounting his tale to his horrified family

pages.caption: Then the girls were very angry with Beauty, and said it was all her fault.
pages.description: [The sisters glaring angrily at Beauty]
pages.scene: The sisters glaring angrily at Beauty

pages.caption: "I have, indeed, caused this misfortune, but I assure you I did it innocently.
pages.description: [Beauty standing bravely before her family]
pages.scene: Beauty standing bravely before her family

pages.caption: I will therefore go back with my father to keep his promise."
pages.description: [Beauty embracing her father, resolved to go back]
pages.scene: Beauty embracing her father, resolved to go back

pages.caption: While they were talking the night fell, and then, to their great surprise, wonderful colored lights began to shine in all directions.
pages.description: [Beauty and her father riding through a forest lit by colorful fireworks]
pages.scene: Beauty and her father riding through a forest lit by colorful fireworks

pages.caption: When they got nearer to the palace they saw that it was illuminated from the roof to the ground, and music sounded softly from the courtyard.
pages.description: [A magnificent palace illuminated from roof to ground]
pages.scene: A magnificent palace illuminated from roof to ground

pages.caption: The merchant led her to the little room he had been in before, where they found a splendid fire burning, and the table daintily spread with a delicious supper.
pages.description: [Beauty entering a small, warm room with a fire and supper]
pages.scene: Beauty entering a small, warm room with a fire and supper

pages.caption: But when the Beast really appeared, though she trembled at the sight of him, she made a great effort to hide her terror, and saluted him respectfully.
pages.description: [The Beast appearing in the doorway as Beauty and her father watch]
pages.scene: The Beast appearing in the doorway as Beauty and her father watch

pages.caption: "Good-evening, old man. Good-evening, Beauty."
pages.description: [The Beast addressing Beauty and the merchant]
pages.scene: The Beast addressing Beauty and the merchant

pages.caption: "Good-evening, Beast," she answered sweetly.
pages.description: [Beauty answering the Beast calmly]
pages.scene: Beauty answering the Beast calmly

pages.caption: "Have you come willingly?" asked the Beast. "Will you be content to stay here when your father goes away?"
pages.description: [The Beast leaning close to Beauty, asking a question]
pages.scene: The Beast leaning close to Beauty, asking a question

pages.caption: Beauty answered bravely that she was quite prepared to stay.
pages.description: [Beauty standing tall and resolute before the Beast]
pages.scene: Beauty standing tall and resolute before the Beast

pages.caption: "As for you, old man," he added, turning to the merchant, "at sunrise to-morrow you will take your departure."
pages.description: [The Beast gesturing toward the merchant, granting him leave]
pages.scene: The Beast gesturing toward the merchant, granting him leave

pages.caption: Then turning to Beauty, he said: "Take your father into the next room, and help him to choose everything you think your brothers and sisters would like to have."
pages.description: [Beauty and her father choosing treasures in a room full of riches]
pages.scene: Beauty and her father choosing treasures in a room full of riches

pages.caption: The merchant was forced to bid Beauty a hasty farewell; and as soon as he was mounted he went off at such a pace that she lost sight of him in an instant.
pages.description: [The merchant saying goodbye to Beauty at the palace steps]
pages.scene: The merchant saying goodbye to Beauty at the palace steps

pages.caption: Then Beauty began to cry, and wandered sadly back to her own room.
pages.description: [Beauty crying alone in her room]
pages.scene: Beauty crying alone in her room

pages.caption: And then she dreamed that she was walking by a brook bordered with trees, when a young prince, handsomer than anyone she had ever seen, came and said to her, "Ah, Beauty! you are not so unfortunate as you suppose."
pages.description: [Beauty walking by a brook in a dream, meeting a handsome prince]
pages.scene: Beauty walking by a brook in a dream, meeting a handsome prince

pages.caption: "Only be grateful," he answered, "and do not trust too much to your eyes. And, above all, do not desert me until you have saved me from my cruel misery."
pages.description: [The prince speaking earnestly to Beauty in the dream]
pages.scene: The prince speaking earnestly to Beauty in the dream

pages.caption: After this she thought she found herself in a room with a stately and beautiful lady, who said to her: "Dear Beauty, try not to regret all you have left behind you, for you are destined to a better fate."
pages.description: [A beautiful lady in a dream, speaking kindly to Beauty]
pages.scene: A beautiful lady in a dream, speaking kindly to Beauty

pages.caption: The first she entered was lined with mirrors, and Beauty saw herself reflected on every side, and thought she had never seen such a charming room.
pages.description: [Beauty waking and finding a mirror-lined room]
pages.scene: Beauty waking and finding a mirror-lined room

pages.caption: A bracelet which was hanging from a chandelier caught her eye, and on taking it down she was greatly surprised to find that it held a portrait of her unknown admirer.
pages.description: [Beauty finding a bracelet with the prince's portrait]
pages.scene: Beauty finding a bracelet with the prince's portrait

pages.caption: The next room was a library, and here she amused herself for a long while in trying some of the instruments, and singing until she was tired.
pages.description: [Beauty sitting in a room full of musical instruments]
pages.scene: Beauty sitting in a room full of musical instruments

pages.caption: This morning she decided to amuse herself in the garden, for the sun shone, and all the fountains were playing; but she was astonished to find that every place was familiar to her.
pages.description: [Beauty gazing out a window at a garden that looks familiar]
pages.scene: Beauty gazing out a window at a garden that looks familiar

pages.caption: There was one room which she had not noticed particularly; it was empty, except that under each of the windows stood a very comfortable chair.
pages.description: [Beauty discovering a room with chairs and windows facing blank curtains]
pages.scene: Beauty discovering a room with chairs and windows facing blank curtains

pages.caption: The first time she had looked out of the window it had seemed to her that a black curtain prevented her from seeing anything outside.
pages.description: [Beauty sitting in a chair as a curtain rises to reveal a dance]
pages.scene: Beauty sitting in a chair as a curtain rises to reveal a dance

pages.caption: But the second time she went into the room, happening to be tired, she sat down in one of the chairs, when instantly the curtain was rolled aside, and a most amusing pantomime was acted before her.
pages.description: [Beauty watching a colorful pantomime from her chair]
pages.scene: Beauty watching a colorful pantomime from her chair

pages.caption: Every evening after supper the Beast came to see her, and always before saying good-night asked her in his terrible voice: "Beauty, will you marry me?"
pages.description: [The Beast appearing at suppertime, asking Beauty a question]
pages.scene: The Beast appearing at suppertime, asking Beauty a question

pages.caption: And it seemed to Beauty, now she understood him better, that when she said, "No, Beast," he went away quite sad.
pages.description: [Beauty looking sadly at the Beast as he turns to leave]
pages.scene: Beauty looking sadly at the Beast as he turns to leave

pages.caption: So everything went on for a long time, until at last, happy as she was, Beauty began to long for the sight of her father and her brothers and sisters.
pages.description: [Beauty gazing out a window, longing for home]
pages.scene: Beauty gazing out a window, longing for home

pages.caption: "Ah! Beauty, have you the heart to desert an unhappy Beast like this?"
pages.description: [The Beast weeping at Beauty's feet]
pages.scene: The Beast weeping at Beauty's feet

pages.caption: "No, dear Beast," answered Beauty softly, "I do not hate you, and I should be very sorry never to see you any more, but I long to see my father again.
pages.description: [Beauty speaking gently to the Beast]
pages.scene: Beauty speaking gently to the Beast

pages.caption: Only say good-by to all your brothers and sisters the night before you come away, and when you have gone to bed turn this ring round upon your finger and say firmly: 'I wish to go back to my palace and see my Beast again.'"
pages.description: [The Beast handing Beauty a ring]
pages.scene: The Beast handing Beauty a ring

pages.caption: As soon as Beauty was alone she hastened to fill the boxes with all the rare and precious things she saw about her.
pages.description: [Beauty packing boxes with treasures]
pages.scene: Beauty packing boxes with treasures

pages.caption: And when at last she did begin to dream of her beloved Prince she was grieved to see him stretched upon a grassy bank, sad and weary, and hardly like himself.
pages.description: [Beauty dreaming of the prince lying sadly on a grassy bank]
pages.scene: Beauty dreaming of the prince lying sadly on a grassy bank

pages.caption: He looked at her reproachfully, and said: "How can you ask me, cruel one? Are you not leaving me to my death perhaps?"
pages.description: [The prince looking at Beauty reproachfully in the dream]
pages.scene: The prince looking at Beauty reproachfully in the dream

pages.caption: And opening her eyes she found herself in a room she had never seen before, which was certainly not nearly so splendid as those she was used to in the Beast's palace.
pages.description: [Beauty waking in her father's cottage, surprised]
pages.scene: Beauty waking in her father's cottage, surprised

pages.caption: She suddenly heard her father's voice, and rushed out and greeted him joyfully.
pages.description: [Beauty rushing joyfully to embrace her father]
pages.scene: Beauty rushing joyfully to embrace her father

pages.caption: But though they were rich now, and lived in town again, and had plenty of acquaintances, Beauty found that nothing amused her very much.
pages.description: [Beauty and her family sitting together, but she looks distracted]
pages.scene: Beauty and her family sitting together, but she looks distracted

pages.caption: Every day when she got up she meant to say it at night, and when night came she put it off again, until at last she had a dismal dream.
pages.description: [Beauty tossing in bed, haunted by a terrible dream]
pages.scene: Beauty tossing in bed, haunted by a terrible dream

pages.caption: She thought she was wandering in a lonely path in the palace gardens, when she heard groans which seemed to come from some bushes hiding the entrance of a cave.
pages.description: [Beauty in a dream, finding the Beast dying in a garden cave]
pages.scene: Beauty in a dream, finding the Beast dying in a garden cave

pages.caption: And at the same moment a stately lady appeared, and said very gravely: "Ah! Beauty, you are only just in time to save his life.
pages.description: [The stately lady from the dream appearing, rebuking Beauty]
pages.scene: The stately lady from the dream appearing, rebuking Beauty

pages.caption: Beauty was so terrified by this dream that the next morning she announced her intention of going back at once.
pages.description: [Beauty waking, determined to return at once]
pages.scene: Beauty waking, determined to return at once

pages.caption: And that very night she said good-by to her father and all her brothers and sisters.
pages.description: [Beauty saying a final goodbye to her family]
pages.scene: Beauty saying a final goodbye to her family

pages.caption: And as soon as she was in bed she turned her ring round upon her finger, and said firmly, "I wish to go back to my palace and see my Beast again."
pages.description: [Beauty turning the ring on her finger and wishing aloud]
pages.scene: Beauty turning the ring on her finger and wishing aloud

pages.caption: Then she fell asleep instantly, and only woke up to hear the clock saying "Beauty, Beauty" twelve times in its musical voice.
pages.description: [Beauty waking to find herself back in the palace]
pages.scene: Beauty waking to find herself back in the palace

pages.caption: Up and down the paths and avenues ran poor Beauty, calling him in vain, for no one answered.
pages.description: [Beauty searching the palace gardens, calling for the Beast]
pages.scene: Beauty searching the palace gardens, calling for the Beast

pages.caption: She rushed down it, and, sure enough, there was the cave, and in it lay the Beast--asleep, as Beauty thought.
pages.description: [Beauty finding the Beast lying motionless in the cave]
pages.scene: Beauty finding the Beast lying motionless in the cave

pages.caption: "Oh! he is dead; and it is all my fault," said Beauty, crying bitterly.
pages.description: [Beauty kneeling over the Beast, weeping]
pages.scene: Beauty kneeling over the Beast, weeping

pages.caption: Hastily fetching some water from the nearest fountain, she sprinkled it over his face, and, to her great delight, he began to revive.
pages.description: [Beauty sprinkling water on the Beast's face]
pages.scene: Beauty sprinkling water on the Beast's face

pages.caption: "Can you really love such an ugly creature as I am?" said the Beast faintly.
pages.description: [The Beast opening his eyes, gazing up at Beauty]
pages.scene: The Beast opening his eyes, gazing up at Beauty

pages.caption: Beauty, who had half expected that he would be angry with her, was reassured by his gentle voice, and went back to the palace.
pages.description: [Beauty sitting with the Beast as he talks gently]
pages.scene: Beauty sitting with the Beast as he talks gently

pages.caption: And when at last the time came for him to go, and he asked, as he had so often asked before, "Beauty, will you marry me?"
pages.description: [The Beast asking Beauty one final time]
pages.scene: The Beast asking Beauty one final time

pages.caption: She answered softly, "Yes, dear Beast."
pages.description: [Beauty speaking softly, with a loving smile]
pages.scene: Beauty speaking softly, with a loving smile

pages.caption: As she spoke a blaze of light sprang up before the windows of the palace; fireworks crackled and guns banged.
pages.description: [Fireworks blazing across the palace windows]
pages.scene: Fireworks blazing across the palace windows

pages.caption: Turning to ask the Beast what it could all mean, Beauty found that he had disappeared, and in his place stood her long-loved Prince!
pages.description: [The Beast vanishing, replaced by a handsome prince]
pages.scene: The Beast vanishing, replaced by a handsome prince

pages.caption: At the same moment the wheels of a chariot were heard upon the terrace, and two ladies entered the room.
pages.description: [Two queens entering the room, one the stately lady from the dream]
pages.scene: Two queens entering the room, one the stately lady from the dream

pages.caption: "Well, Queen, this is Beauty, who has had the courage to rescue your son from the terrible enchantment.
pages.description: [The stately lady presenting Beauty to the queen]
pages.scene: The stately lady presenting Beauty to the queen

pages.caption: "I consent with all my heart," cried the Queen. "How can I ever thank you enough, charming girl, for having restored my dear son to his natural form?"
pages.description: [The queen embracing Beauty and the Prince]
pages.scene: The queen embracing Beauty and the Prince

pages.caption: "Now," said the Fairy to Beauty, "I suppose you would like me to send for all your brothers and sisters to dance at your wedding?"
pages.description: [The fairy offering to bring Beauty's family]
pages.scene: The fairy offering to bring Beauty's family

pages.caption: And so she did, and the marriage was celebrated the very next day with the utmost splendor.
pages.description: [Beauty and the Prince married in a grand celebration]
pages.scene: Beauty and the Prince married in a grand celebration

pages.caption: And Beauty and the Prince lived happily ever after.
pages.description: [Beauty and the Prince together, happy forever after]
pages.scene: Beauty and the Prince together, happy forever after
